                      [32m'The admin dashboard is available at `http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/`.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The authentication system in pocketbase-async handles user identification and session management through JSON Web Tokens (JWTs).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It provides methods to authenticate users and admins, automatically refreshes expired tokens, and maintains authentication state across requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Pocketbase - CodingKiwi\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-04, last updated: 2026-06-14, [Read more](https://blog.coding.kiwi/pocketbase/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"With **realtime events**, the server sends an event whenever something changes; I'll cover that in more detail later.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Pocketbase offers realtime subscriptions to collection changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can subscribe to all track changes like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Internally, the JS SDK only subscribes to the tracks once, even if you subscribe to track changes in different parts of your app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, this means that if you call `unsubscribe` inside `onUnmounted`, it kills the subscription for *all* other places in the app listening for those changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is important to only unsubscribe from the specific listener; luckily, the `subscribe` method returns an `unsubscribe` callback for this purpose.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's say we want a live list of all tracks in a folder.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It is possible to subscribe with a filter:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await pb.collection("tracks").subscribe("*", e => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter: "folder = null"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//created subscription:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The issue is that if a track changes and no longer matches this filter (because the folder of the track changed), the subscription isn't triggered, so I don't receive an update or delete event.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'My current solution is to listen to the entire collection and check if the change matters:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# realtime subscription: events for items that no longer match filter · pocketbase/pocketbase · Discussion #6901\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-06-02, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/6901)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Both subscriptions work correctly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Event for the "transient" state was considered in the past but after some experimentation was discarded due to some rough edges.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The only workaround I can think of at the moment is to maintain the party join status in a separate collection (e.g. `partyUsers`) with 2 single relation fields pointing to the party and user *(the user field can have a unique constraint defined to prevent joining multiple parties at the same time)*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Maybe add an `OnRecordUpdateRequest` hook on `users` collection?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// fires only for "users" records\n'[39m +
                      [32m'onRecordAfterUpdateSuccess((e) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// e.app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// e.record\n'[39m +
                      [32m'e.next()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (e.record.get("party") == null && e.record.original.get("party") != null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for (let client of e.app.subscriptionsBroker().clients()) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// enumerate all clients who have subscribed "party=xxx" on "users"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}, "users")\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Feature Request: @request.query.* for realtime API #2514\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-05-19, last updated: 2025-10-26, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/issues/2514)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Realtime Subscriptions — PocketBase Cloud Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-26, [Read more](https://pocketbasecloud.com/docs/pocketbase/realtime-subscriptions/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PocketBase includes realtime out of the box: your app can subscribe to a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection (or a single record) and receive create, update, and delete events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the moment they happen.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Under the hood it uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), which\n'[39m +
                      [32m'works through PocketBase Cloud’s HTTPS proxy with no extra setup.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.collection("messages").subscribe("*", (e) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (e.action === "create") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'messages.push(e.record);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (e.action === "update") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const i = messages.findIndex((m) => m.id === e.record.id);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (i >= 0) messages[i] = e.record;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (e.action === "delete") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'messages = messages.filter((m) => m.id !== e.record.id);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Events are only delivered for records the connected client is allowed to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**view** according to the collection’s API rules.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Subscriptions also support filters and expand options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.collection("messages").subscribe(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(e) => { /* ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/ },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m`filter: "room = 'lobby'",\n`[39m +
                      [32m'expand: "author",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# PocketBase JavaScript SDK\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-08-01, last updated: 2025-09-13, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/js-sdk)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// for server: npm install eventsource --save\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.filter(expr, params)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'requestKey: null|string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Subscribe to realtime changes to the specified topic ("*" or recordId).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.collection(collectionIdOrName).subscribe(topic, callback, options = {});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all registered subscriptions to the specified topic ("*" or recordId).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// If topic is not set, then it will remove all registered collection subscriptions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.collection(collectionIdOrName).unsubscribe([topic]);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Returns the first found collection matching the specified filter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔐 pb.collections.getFirstListItem(filter, options = {});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Initialize the realtime connection (if not already) and register the subscription listener.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// You can subscribe to the `PB_CONNECT` event if you want to listen to the realtime connection connect/reconnect events.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.subscribe(topic, callback, options = {});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all subscription listeners with the specified topic.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all subscription listeners starting with the specified topic prefix.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all subscriptions matching the specified topic and listener function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.unsubscribeByTopicAndListener(topic, callback);'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction - API rules and filters - Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-16, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-rules-and-filters/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Used to access the current request data, such as query parameters, body/form fields, authorized user state, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `**@collection.***`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This filter could be used to target other collections that are not directly related to the current\n'[39m +
                      [32m'one (aka. there is no relation field pointing to it) but both shares a common field value, like\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for example a category id:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@collection.news.categoryId ?= categoryId && @collection.news.author ?= @request.auth.id`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you want to join the same collection multiple times but based on different criteria, you\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can define an alias by appending `:alias` suffix to the collection name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The syntax basically follows the format\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`OPERAND OPERATOR OPERAND`, where:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != ""`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users and return records that are either "active" or "pending":\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && (status = "active" || status = "pending")`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users who are listed in an *allowed_users* multi-relation field value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && allowed_users.id ?= @request.auth.id`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Web APIs reference - API Realtime - Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-11, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-realtime/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Realtime API is implemented via Server-Sent Events (SSE).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generally, it consists of 2 operations:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. establish SSE connection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. submit client subscriptions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SSE events are sent for **create**, **update** and **delete** record operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**You could subscribe to a single record or to an entire collection.**\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When you subscribe to a **single record**, the collection's **ViewRule** will be used to determine whether the subscriber has access to receive the event message.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"When you subscribe to an **entire collection**, the collection's **ListRule** will be used to determine whether the subscriber has access to receive the event message.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'All of this is seamlessly handled by the SDKs using just the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'subscribe\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'unsubscribe\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'methods:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"pb.collection('example').subscribe('*', function (e) {\n"[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(e.action);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(e.record);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}, { /* other options like expand, custom headers, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/ });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Subscribe to changes only in the specified record\n'[39m +
                      [32m"pb.collection('example').subscribe('RECORD_ID', function (e) {\n"[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(e.action);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(e.record);'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Introduction - How to use PocketBase - Docs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The access and filter controls for your data are usually done through the collection API rules .\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### EventSource Polyfill (Realtime Subscriptions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Node.js does not have a native `EventSource` implementation, which is required for realtime subscriptions.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'**EventSource Detection**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `RealtimeService` requires `EventSource`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If unavailable (Node.js), instantiation fails unless a polyfill is registered globally:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When using the PocketBase SDK in Node.js:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. **Install** via npm and import as ESM or CJS\n'[39m +

                      [32m'5. **Use cookie methods** (`loadFromCookie`, `exportToCookie`) for SSR persistence\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2024-05-08, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/4882)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Remove the first wrapping quotes, aka.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'it must be:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// or filter: pb.filter("features={:id}", { id: filters })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter: `features="${filters}"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you are receiving an empty list then either your request doesn't satisfy the List API rule of your collection or your provided filter doesn't match any record.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Side-note: if `features` is a multiple `relation` field then comparing it to a single id string will not work because it is represented as serialized json array.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For this case you can use dot-nation to target explicitly the `id` field of the `relation` records, eg.:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'filter: searchIds.map((id) => pb.filter("features.id ?= {:id}", { id })).join("||")\n'[39m +

                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# pocketbase\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-08-01, last updated: 2026-07-13, [Read more](https://app.unpkg.com/pocketbase@0.21.5/files/README.md)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Caveats ### Binding filter parameters The SDK comes with a helper `pb.filter(expr, params)` method to generate a filter string with placeholder parameters (`{:paramName}`) populated from an object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**This method is also recommended when using the SDK in Node/Deno/Bun server-side list queries and accepting untrusted user input as `filter` string arguments, because it will take care to properly escape the generated string expression, avoiding eventual string inje\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ction attacks** (_on the client-side this is not much of an issue_).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```js const records = await pb.collection("example").getList(1, 20, { // the same as: "title ~ \'te\\\\\'st\' && (totalA = 123 || totalB = 123)" filter: pb.filter("title ~ {:title} && (totalA = {:num} || totalB = {:num})", { title: "te\'st", num: 123 }) }) ``` The supported placeholder parameter values are: - `string` (_single quotes are autoescaped_) - `number` - `boolean` - `Date` object (_will be stringified into the format expected by Pocket\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Filtering a list using an array · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #1509\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-06, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/1509)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you are asking for how to exclude an array of ids as part of a filter expression you can combine multiple conditions with the `||` (or) or `&&` (and) operators, eg. something like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const idsToExclude = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id1",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id2",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id3"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'];\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const conditions = idsToExclude.map((id) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return `myField != "${id}"`;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m"await pb.collection('example').getList(1, 50, {\n"[39m +
                      [32m'filter: conditions.join("&&"),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If `immoId` is a `text` or `relation` field then you need to wrap your values with single or double quotes, aka:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"immoId != '12341425' && immoId != '12341426'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The double quotes did it!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`var conditions = itemIds.map((id) => 'immoId != "$id"');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction - API rules and filters - Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-16, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-rules-and-filters/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The syntax basically follows the format\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`OPERAND OPERATOR OPERAND`, where:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `OPERAND` - could be any field literal, string (single or double quoted),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'number, null, true, false\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `OPERATOR` - is one of:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `=` Equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `!=` NOT equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `>` Greater than\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `>=` Greater than or equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `<` Less than\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `<=` Less than or equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `~` Like/Contains (if not specified auto wraps the right string OPERAND in a "%" for wildcard match)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To group and combine several expressions you can use parenthesis\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Efficient way to filter by list of values · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #1823\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-10, last updated: 2025-07-09, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/1823)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'operator is one way to do it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Alternatively, as you noted, you can combine the conditions with multiple\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'||\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'statements:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'?filter=(sku = "sku1" || sku = "sku2" || sku = "sku3")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// OR programmatically you can create the above expression like this (_js example_):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const skus = ["sku1", "sku2", "sku3"];\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const result = await pb.collection('reviews').getList(1, 20, {\n"[39m +
                      [32m"sort: '-creation_date',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'filter: skus.map((sku) => `sku="${sku}"`).join("||"),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# How to query for the contents of a multiple relation? · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #6423\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You should be able to use dot-notation to target the specific posts, something like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'let searchTag = "myTag";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const posts = await pb.collection("posts").getFullList({\n'[39m +
                      [32m`// the same as "tags.title ?= 'myTag'"\n`[39m +
                      [32m'filter: pb.filter("tags.title ?= {:tag}", { tag: searchTag }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(for all operators you could read https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-rules-and-filters/#filters-syntax).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'let searchTag = "myTag";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const posts = await pb.collection("posts").getFullList({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Web APIs reference - API Realtime - Docs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Realtime API is implemented via Server-Sent Events (SSE).\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Realtime Events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-09, [Read more](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/realtime)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When using PocketBase in hooks or PocketPages (server-side), you cannot subscribe to realtime events since the JSVM environment doesn't support WebSocket connections.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In client-side code, you can use the full PocketBase JavaScript SDK to both send and receive realtime events:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The PocketBase JS SDK automatically handles connection management:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Automatically reconnects when the connection is lost\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Resubscribes to previous channels after reconnection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Provides connection status via `pb.realtime.isConnected`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also listen for disconnect events:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.realtime.onDisconnect = function (activeSubscriptions) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"console.log('Disconnected with active subscriptions:', activeSubscriptions)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Optionally handle the disconnect event\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// The client will automatically attempt to reconnect\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Server (JSVM) can only send events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Clients can both send and receive events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Use the appropriate SDK for each environment\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. **SDK Versions**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Browser/Node.js: Use pocketbase/js-sdk\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Server/JSVM: Use pocketbase-js-sdk-jsvm\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. **Best Practices**'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you keep the SSE connection open longer than 5 mins? · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #3054\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-08-02, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/3054)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> If the connected client doesn't receive any new messages for 5 minutes, the server will send a disconnect signal (this is to prevent forgotten/leaked connections).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The connection will be automatically reestablished if the client is still active (eg. the browser tab is still open).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So pocketbase will attempt to keep the conenction live, it will close it and re-open it, essentially allowing an 'indefinite' connection\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the connection with the server is broken the SDKs will try to perform autoreconnect behind the scene indefinitely on various intervals (200ms, 300ms, 500ms, etc. it will depend on the SSE implementation).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Users usually shouldn't do anything in addition.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The JS SDK has a helper `pb.realtime.isConnected` getter that could be used to determine whether an SSE connection was established.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The Dart SDK currently doesn't have such helper exposed but I guess you can check if `pb.realtime.clientId` is non-empty.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to know when the SSE connection was established (initially or on reconnect), you can subscribe to the `PB_CONNECT` event, aka.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`pb.realtime.subscribe("PB_CONNECT", ...)`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# pocketbase\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-09, last updated: 2026-07-02, [Read more](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/package/pocketbase)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Official JavaScript SDK (browser and node) for interacting with the PocketBase API.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> 🔧 Node doesn't have native `EventSource` implementation, so in order to use the realtime subscriptions you'll need to load a `EventSource` polyfill.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Initialize the realtime connection (if not already) and register the subscription listener.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// You can subscribe to the `PB_CONNECT` event if you want to listen to the realtime connection connect/reconnect events.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.subscribe(topic, callback, options = {});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all subscription listeners with the specified topic.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.unsubscribe(topic?);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Getter that checks whether the realtime connection has been established.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.realtime.isConnected\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// An optional hook that is invoked when the realtime client disconnects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// either when unsubscribing from all subscriptions or when the connection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// was interrupted or closed by the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Note that the realtime client autoreconnect on its own and this hook is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// useful only for the cases where you want to apply a special behavior on\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// server error or after closing the realtime connection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.realtime.onDisconnect = function(activeSubscriptions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                  [32m"const pb = new PocketBase('http://127.0.0.1:8090');\n"[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The admin dashboard is available at `http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/`.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Pocketbase - CodingKiwi\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-04, last updated: 2026-06-14, [Read more](https://blog.coding.kiwi/pocketbase/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"With **realtime events**, the server sends an event whenever something changes; I'll cover that in more detail later.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Pocketbase offers realtime subscriptions to collection changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can subscribe to all track changes like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Internally, the JS SDK only subscribes to the tracks once, even if you subscribe to track changes in different parts of your app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, this means that if you call `unsubscribe` inside `onUnmounted`, it kills the subscription for *all* other places in the app listening for those changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is important to only unsubscribe from the specific listener; luckily, the `subscribe` method returns an `unsubscribe` callback for this purpose.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's say we want a live list of all tracks in a folder.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It is possible to subscribe with a filter:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await pb.collection("tracks").subscribe("*", e => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'//created subscription:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The issue is that if a track changes and no longer matches this filter (because the folder of the track changed), the subscription isn't triggered, so I don't receive an update or delete event.\n"[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Realtime Subscriptions — PocketBase Cloud Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-26, [Read more](https://pocketbasecloud.com/docs/pocketbase/realtime-subscriptions/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PocketBase includes realtime out of the box: your app can subscribe to a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection (or a single record) and receive create, update, and delete events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the moment they happen.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Under the hood it uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), which\n'[39m +
                      [32m'works through PocketBase Cloud’s HTTPS proxy with no extra setup.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.collection("messages").subscribe("*", (e) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (e.action === "create") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'messages.push(e.record);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (e.action === "update") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const i = messages.findIndex((m) => m.id === e.record.id);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (i >= 0) messages[i] = e.record;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (e.action === "delete") {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'messages = messages.filter((m) => m.id !== e.record.id);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Events are only delivered for records the connected client is allowed to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**view** according to the collection’s API rules.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Subscriptions also support filters and expand options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.collection("messages").subscribe(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(e) => { /* ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/ },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m`filter: "room = 'lobby'",\n`[39m +
                      [32m'expand: "author",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Used to access the current request data, such as query parameters, body/form fields, authorized user state, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `**@collection.***`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This filter could be used to target other collections that are not directly related to the current\n'[39m +
                      [32m'one (aka. there is no relation field pointing to it) but both shares a common field value, like\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for example a category id:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@collection.news.categoryId ?= categoryId && @collection.news.author ?= @request.auth.id`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you want to join the same collection multiple times but based on different criteria, you\n'[39m +
                      [32m'can define an alias by appending `:alias` suffix to the collection name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The syntax basically follows the format\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`OPERAND OPERATOR OPERAND`, where:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != ""`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users and return records that are either "active" or "pending":\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && (status = "active" || status = "pending")`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users who are listed in an *allowed_users* multi-relation field value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && allowed_users.id ?= @request.auth.id`'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Web APIs reference - API Realtime - Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-11, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-realtime/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Realtime API is implemented via Server-Sent Events (SSE).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generally, it consists of 2 operations:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. establish SSE connection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. submit client subscriptions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SSE events are sent for **create**, **update** and **delete** record operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**You could subscribe to a single record or to an entire collection.**\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When you subscribe to a **single record**, the collection's **ViewRule** will be used to determine whether the subscriber has access to receive the event message.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"When you subscribe to an **entire collection**, the collection's **ListRule** will be used to determine whether the subscriber has access to receive the event message.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'All of this is seamlessly handled by the SDKs using just the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'subscribe\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'#### 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Node.js 环境中的实时订阅问题\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**问题描述：**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'在 Node.js 环境中，新手可能会遇到实时订阅功能无法正常工作的问题，因为 Node.js 默认不支持 `EventSource`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**解决步骤：**\n'[39m +

                      [32m'global.EventSource = eventsource;\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### EventSource Polyfill (Realtime Subscriptions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Node.js does not have a native `EventSource` implementation, which is required for realtime subscriptions.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The `RealtimeService` requires `EventSource`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If unavailable (Node.js), instantiation fails unless a polyfill is registered globally:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When using the PocketBase SDK in Node.js:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. **Install** via npm and import as ESM or CJS\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. **Add polyfills** for Node < 17 (`cross-fetch`) and realtime (`eventsource`)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'5. **Use cookie methods** (`loadFromCookie`, `exportToCookie`) for SSR persistence\n'[39m +
                      [32m'6. **Reference** Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for framework-specific patterns'[39m

                      [32m'created: 2024-05-08, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/4882)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Remove the first wrapping quotes, aka.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'it must be:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// or filter: pb.filter("features={:id}", { id: filters })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter: `features="${filters}"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you are receiving an empty list then either your request doesn't satisfy the List API rule of your collection or your provided filter doesn't match any record.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Side-note: if `features` is a multiple `relation` field then comparing it to a single id string will not work because it is represented as serialized json array.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For this case you can use dot-nation to target explicitly the `id` field of the `relation` records, eg.:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m"expand: 'features'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# pocketbase\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-08-01, last updated: 2026-07-13, [Read more](https://app.unpkg.com/pocketbase@0.21.5/files/README.md)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Caveats ### Binding filter parameters The SDK comes with a helper `pb.filter(expr, params)` method to generate a filter string with placeholder parameters (`{:paramName}`) populated from an object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**This method is also recommended when using the SDK in Node/Deno/Bun server-side list queries and accepting untrusted user input as `filter` string arguments, because it will take care to properly escape the generated string expression, avoiding eventual string inje\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ction attacks** (_on the client-side this is not much of an issue_).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```js const records = await pb.collection("example").getList(1, 20, { // the same as: "title ~ \'te\\\\\'st\' && (totalA = 123 || totalB = 123)" filter: pb.filter("title ~ {:title} && (totalA = {:num} || totalB = {:num})", { title: "te\'st", num: 123 }) }) ``` The supported placeholder parameter values are: - `string` (_single quotes are autoescaped_) - `number` - `boolean` - `Date` object (_will be stringified into the format expected by Pocket\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Filtering a list using an array · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #1509\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-06, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/1509)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you are asking for how to exclude an array of ids as part of a filter expression you can combine multiple conditions with the `||` (or) or `&&` (and) operators, eg. something like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const idsToExclude = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id1",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id2",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"id3"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'];\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const conditions = idsToExclude.map((id) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return `myField != "${id}"`;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m"await pb.collection('example').getList(1, 50, {\n"[39m +
                      [32m'filter: conditions.join("&&"),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If `immoId` is a `text` or `relation` field then you need to wrap your values with single or double quotes, aka:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"immoId != '12341425' && immoId != '12341426'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The double quotes did it!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`var conditions = itemIds.map((id) => 'immoId != "$id"');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction - API rules and filters - Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-16, [Read more](https://pocketbase.io/docs/api-rules-and-filters/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The syntax basically follows the format\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`OPERAND OPERATOR OPERAND`, where:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `OPERAND` - could be any field literal, string (single or double quoted),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'number, null, true, false\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `OPERATOR` - is one of:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `=` Equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `!=` NOT equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `>` Greater than\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `>=` Greater than or equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `<` Less than\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `<=` Less than or equal\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `~` Like/Contains (if not specified auto wraps the right string OPERAND in a "%" for wildcard match)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To group and combine several expressions you can use parenthesis\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`(...)`, `&&` (AND) and `||` (OR) tokens.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != ""`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users and return records that are either "active" or "pending":\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && (status = "active" || status = "pending")`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Allow only registered users who are listed in an *allowed_users* multi-relation field value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@request.auth.id != "" && allowed_users.id ?= @request.auth.id`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Efficient way to filter by list of values · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #1823\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-10, last updated: 2025-07-09, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/1823)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'operator is one way to do it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Alternatively, as you noted, you can combine the conditions with multiple\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'||\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'statements:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'?filter=(sku = "sku1" || sku = "sku2" || sku = "sku3")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// OR programmatically you can create the above expression like this (_js example_):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const skus = ["sku1", "sku2", "sku3"];\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const result = await pb.collection('reviews').getList(1, 20, {\n"[39m +
                      [32m"sort: '-creation_date',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'filter: skus.map((sku) => `sku="${sku}"`).join("||"),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'||\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'approach may be slightly better, since it will be translated directly to the SQL:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"sku='sku1' OR sku='sku2' OR sku='sku3'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m', while the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Realtime Events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-09, [Read more](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/realtime)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When using PocketBase in hooks or PocketPages (server-side), you cannot subscribe to realtime events since the JSVM environment doesn't support WebSocket connections.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In client-side code, you can use the full PocketBase JavaScript SDK to both send and receive realtime events:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The PocketBase JS SDK automatically handles connection management:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Automatically reconnects when the connection is lost\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Resubscribes to previous channels after reconnection\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- Clients can both send and receive events\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Use the appropriate SDK for each environment\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. **SDK Versions**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Browser/Node.js: Use pocketbase/js-sdk\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Server/JSVM: Use pocketbase-js-sdk-jsvm\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. **Best Practices**'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you keep the SSE connection open longer than 5 mins? · pocketbase pocketbase · Discussion #3054\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-08-02, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/3054)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> If the connected client doesn't receive any new messages for 5 minutes, the server will send a disconnect signal (this is to prevent forgotten/leaked connections).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The connection will be automatically reestablished if the client is still active (eg. the browser tab is still open).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So pocketbase will attempt to keep the conenction live, it will close it and re-open it, essentially allowing an 'indefinite' connection\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the connection with the server is broken the SDKs will try to perform autoreconnect behind the scene indefinitely on various intervals (200ms, 300ms, 500ms, etc. it will depend on the SSE implementation).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Users usually shouldn't do anything in addition.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The JS SDK has a helper `pb.realtime.isConnected` getter that could be used to determine whether an SSE connection was established.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The Dart SDK currently doesn't have such helper exposed but I guess you can check if `pb.realtime.clientId` is non-empty.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to know when the SSE connection was established (initially or on reconnect), you can subscribe to the `PB_CONNECT` event, aka.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`pb.realtime.subscribe("PB_CONNECT", ...)`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# pocketbase\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-09, last updated: 2026-07-02, [Read more](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/package/pocketbase)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Official JavaScript SDK (browser and node) for interacting with the PocketBase API.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"> 🔧 Node doesn't have native `EventSource` implementation, so in order to use the realtime subscriptions you'll need to load a `EventSource` polyfill.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Initialize the realtime connection (if not already) and register the subscription listener.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// You can subscribe to the `PB_CONNECT` event if you want to listen to the realtime connection connect/reconnect events.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.subscribe(topic, callback, options = {});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Unsubscribe from all subscription listeners with the specified topic.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🔓 pb.realtime.unsubscribe(topic?);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Getter that checks whether the realtime connection has been established.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pb.realtime.isConnected\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// An optional hook that is invoked when the realtime client disconnects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// either when unsubscribing from all subscriptions or when the connection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// was interrupted or closed by the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// useful only for the cases where you want to apply a special behavior on\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// server error or after closing the realtime connection.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Realtime API Documentation | pocketbase/site | DeepWiki\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-01-16, last updated: 2026-07-15, [Read more](https://deepwiki.com/pocketbase/site/4.5-realtime-api-documentation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Event|Trigger|Behavior|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|--|--|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**Auto-disconnect**|No messages received for 5 minutes|Server sends disconnect signal|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**Auto-reconnect**|Client still active after disconnect|Connection automatically reestablished|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**Client closure**|Browser tab closed or explicit disconnect|Connection terminated|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### SDK Method Signatures\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Method|Parameters|Behavior|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`unsubscribe(topic?)`|topic: optional string|Removes subscription(s), disconnects if no subscriptions remain|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### JavaScript SDK Example\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The SDK handles:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Automatic SSE connection establishment on first `subscribe()`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Sending client ID and subscription array via POST\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Reconnection on disconnects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Callback invocation with `{action, record}` event data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Proper cleanup on `unsubscribe()`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To prevent forgotten or leaked connections:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Server tracks activity on each SSE connection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. If no events are sent for **5 minutes**, server initiates disconnect\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. If client is still active (browser tab open), SDK automatically reconnects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. New client ID is issued, subscriptions are resubmitted\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default PocketBase sends realtime events only for Record create/update/delete operations (*and for the OAuth2 auth redirect*), but you are free to send custom realtime messages to the connected clients via the `$app.subscriptionsBroker()` instance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`$app.subscriptionsBroker().clients()` returns all connected `subscriptions.Client` indexed by their unique connection id.\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'if (!chatId) {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const email = process.env.PB_ADMIN_EMAIL;\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  process.exit(1);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'}\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m"const pb = new PocketBase('http://127.0.0.1:8090');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Handle graceful shutdown\n'[39m +
                  [32m'let isShuttingDown = false;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const cleanup = async () => {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (isShuttingDown) return;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  isShuttingDown = true;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  try {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // Unsubscribe from all topics on messages collection to close subscription and SSE connection\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  } finally {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'};\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Create the commit with a message ending with:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'Commit message here.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
